name: Microsoft 365 Assessment tool
what: An open-source command-line tool from the Microsoft PnP community that scans a SharePoint Online tenant and produces CSV files and a Power BI report. Its modules cover classic pages, InfoPath Forms Services, SharePoint Add-ins and Azure ACS, and SharePoint Alerts, so you can see what legacy customisation still exists before Microsoft retires it.
when: Before a SharePoint retirement deadline, for example the block on classic publishing sites from 1 March 2027 and classic user-created pages becoming read-only from 1 October 2028, to find which sites and pages are affected and who owns them.
example: Download the latest release from GitHub (v1.17.0 at the time of checking; the classic pages module needs 1.15.0 or later, and the audit-based usage data 1.16.0 or later).
Register an Entra app with read-only Sites.Read.All (Microsoft Graph and SharePoint, application permissions) and a certificate, and grant admin consent.

Start a small scope first: `microsoft365-assessment.exe start --mode Classic --classicinclude Pages --authmode application --tenant <tenant>.sharepoint.com --applicationid <app-id> --certpath "My|CurrentUser|<thumbprint>" --siteslist "https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/sites/site1"`.

Follow progress with `microsoft365-assessment.exe status`; when the run has finished, generate the Power BI report and CSV files with `microsoft365-assessment.exe report --id <assessment-id>` (find the id with the list command), start with classicpages.csv, then widen the scope to the whole tenant.
pitfalls: Delegated (interactive or device) runs only see the sites the signed-in account can access; use application authentication for a full-tenant picture.
Audit-based page usage needs an extra Microsoft Graph audit permission and is not available in GCC High, DoD or 21Vianet; use --skipusageinformation there.
A high MappingPercentage only means each web part has a mapping; it does not guarantee the transformed page keeps all behaviour.
Large tenants get throttled: start with 4 to 8 threads and run at most a few assessments in parallel.
Run it only against tenants you administer or have written permission to assess.
